title: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: submit, block and start automated investigations from advanced hunting
summary: The briefing's actions, permissions, licensing and roadmap details are supported, including the updated custom-role documentation. Minor corrections should complete two control paths and qualify the beta API, configurable allow-entry lifetime and auditing default.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Selecting query results and Take actions allows analysts to submit false-positive or false-negative emails to Microsoft.
claims.quote: Submit to Microsoft - select this action to submit false positive or false negative emails to Microsoft.

claims.claim: A hunting submission can add URLs and URL domains to the Tenant Allow/Block List while Microsoft evaluates it.
claims.quote: As part of the submission, you can also add URLs and URL domains, sender domains, and file attachments to the Tenant Allow/Block List to immediately mitigate the reported false positive or false negative while Microsoft evaluates the submission.

claims.claim: A hunting submission can add sender domains to the Tenant Allow/Block List.
claims.quote: As part of the submission, you can also add URLs and URL domains, sender domains, and file attachments to the Tenant Allow/Block List

claims.claim: A hunting submission can add file attachments to the Tenant Allow/Block List.
claims.quote: As part of the submission, you can also add URLs and URL domains, sender domains, and file attachments to the Tenant Allow/Block List

claims.claim: Initiate automated investigation starts an investigation on email, sender, recipient or contact recipients.
claims.quote: Initiate automated investigation - select this action to trigger Automated investigation on email, sender, recipient, or contact recipients.

claims.claim: The documented email actions also apply to custom detections.
claims.quote: The email remediation actions described in this section also apply to custom detections.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Analysts can provide an action name and description to track it in Action center history.
claims.quote: You can provide a remediation name and a short description of the action to track it in the action center history.

claims.claim: The wizard provides an Approval ID that can filter the actions in the Action center.
claims.quote: Use the Approval ID provided at the end of the wizard to filter for these actions in the action center

claims.claim: The advanced hunting action reference warns that some information relates to a prereleased product.
claims.quote: Some information in this article relates to a prereleased product which may be substantially modified before it's commercially released.

claims.where: What's changing: three more actions; Risk assessment: existing submission route
claims.claim: These actions extend an existing submission and response route to advanced hunting rather than inventing new underlying operations.
claims.quote: These actions, previously only available in Threat Explorer, are now accessible via custom queries in Advanced Hunting

claims.where: What's changing: definition of advanced hunting
claims.claim: Advanced hunting is a query-based threat-hunting tool in the Microsoft Defender portal.
claims.quote: Advanced hunting is a query-based threat hunting tool
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-overview to sources for the definition of advanced hunting.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Tenant Allow/Block List entries govern organisation-level mail filtering rather than only the analyst's mailbox.
claims.quote: Users in the organization can't send email to these blocked domains and addresses.

claims.claim: An allow entry from a submission skips the filters associated with the allowed entity.
claims.quote: all filters associated with the allowed entities are skipped

claims.claim: Messages containing an allowed entity are delivered if they pass the other filtering-stack checks.
claims.quote: During mail flow or time of click, if messages containing the entities in the allow entries pass other checks in the filtering stack, the messages are delivered

claims.claim: A block entry prevents delivery of mail containing the blocked entity across the organisation.
claims.quote: Email messages that contain file block entries are blocked as malware. Messages containing blocked file entries are quarantined.

claims.where: Why it matters: no Microsoft source says anything changes for users
claims.claim: Microsoft does not describe an automatic change to ordinary users' behaviour when these analyst actions arrive.
claims.quote: Searched: advanced hunting Submit to Microsoft Initiate automated investigation enable disable administrator setting licensing price per action. Read advanced-hunting-take-action and defender-for-office-365-whats-new, October 2025; both describe analyst-selected actions, not automatic user changes.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: an authorised analyst chooses the actions in the wizard.
claims.quote: Select the records you want to take action on, select Take actions, and then under Choose actions, select your choice from the following options

claims.claim: Taking action on emails in advanced hunting requires a Defender for Office 365 role able to search and purge emails, or the documented unified RBAC permissions.
claims.quote: To take action on emails through advanced hunting, you need a role in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 to search and purge emails.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Email & collaboration advanced actions (manage) is a documented unified RBAC permission for taking email actions from advanced hunting.
claims.quote: Security operations > Security data > Email & collaboration advanced actions (manage): Required to take actions on emails (move, soft delete, hard delete).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Response (manage) is also documented for advanced hunting actions and approving or dismissing remediation.
claims.quote: Security operations > Security data > Response (manage): Required to approve or dismiss remediation actions.

claims.claim: The Defender for Office 365 unified RBAC reference maps submitting messages to Microsoft to Response (manage).
claims.quote: | Submit messages to Microsoft | Response (manage) |

claims.claim: Managing Tenant Allow/Block List entries requires Detection tuning (manage) under unified RBAC.
claims.quote: | Manage Tenant Allow/Block List entries | Detection tuning (manage) |

claims.claim: AIR queues recommended threat-remediation actions for security personnel to approve.
claims.quote: When AIR identifies threats, it queues threat remediation actions for SecOps personnel to approve.

claims.claim: AIR automatically approves the pending remediation actions it generates for malicious URL and file clusters.
claims.quote: The auto-remediation capabilities in AIR fully automate the remediation of malicious similarity clusters, including malicious URL and file clusters. For these cluster types, AIR automatically approves the pending remediation actions it generates

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Security personnel can approve or reject other pending AIR actions in the Action center.
claims.quote: Approve: Initiate the pending action. ... Reject: Prevent the pending action from being taken.

claims.claim: Domain and email-address, file and URL block entries expire after 30 days by default.
claims.quote: By default, the following types of block entries expire after 30 days, but you can set them to expire up to 90 days or to never expire

claims.claim: Allow entries for these entity types are kept for 45 days after the filtering system determines the entity is clean.
claims.quote: By default, allow entries for domains and email addresses, files, and URLs are kept for 45 days after the filtering system determines that the entity is clean, and then the allow entry is removed. Or you can set allow entries to expire up to 30 days after you create them.
claims.fix: Replace the clause with 'and, by default, keeps allow entries for these entity types for 45 days after the filtering system determines that the entity is clean'. The lifetime is configurable.

claims.claim: Blocking a URL or URL domain requires joining the URL information table.
claims.quote: To block a URL or URL domain, join the EmailUrlInfo table with NetworkMessageId to get the required details.

claims.claim: Permissions > Microsoft Defender XDR > Roles > Create custom role > Choose permissions > Security operations reaches the custom-role permission area in the Defender portal.
claims.quote: On the Permissions page, under Microsoft Defender XDR, select Roles > Create custom role. ... On the Choose permissions page ... Security operations
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Permissions > Microsoft Defender XDR > Roles > Create custom role > Choose permissions > Security operations > Security data > Email & collaboration advanced actions (manage)'. Retain the note to select Response (manage) in the same section; the final hierarchy is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-take-action.

claims.claim: POST /beta/roleManagement/defender/roleAssignments assigns principals to an existing role using roleDefinitionId and principalIds.
claims.quote: To create role assignment for a Defender provider: POST /roleManagement/defender/roleAssignments ... "roleDefinitionId": "c2cf284d-6c41-4e6b-afac-4b80928c9034", "principalIds":
claims.fix: Append to controls[0].note: 'This Microsoft Graph API is beta, subject to change and not supported for production applications.'

claims.claim: The Defender portal enforces unified RBAC permissions and assignments once unified RBAC is activated.
claims.quote: For the Microsoft Defender portal to start enforcing the permissions and assignments configured in your new or imported roles, you need to activate the new Microsoft Defender unified RBAC model.

claims.claim: The AIR reference applies unified RBAC when Email & collaboration > Defender for Office 365 permissions is Active.
claims.quote: If Email & collaboration > Defender for Office 365 permissions is Active.

claims.claim: Unified RBAC applies to the Defender portal, not PowerShell.

claims.claim: Under Email & collaboration permissions, starting an investigation requires a listed role group such as Security Administrator or Security Operator plus Search and Purge.
claims.quote: Membership in the Organization Management, Security Administrator, Security Operator, Security Reader, or Global Reader role groups. ... The Search and Purge role

claims.claim: Actions & submissions > Action center > Pending reaches the pending AIR action list in the Defender portal.
claims.quote: go to the Pending tab on the Action center page at Actions & submissions > Action center > Pending tab.

claims.claim: An API or PowerShell operation for approving or rejecting Defender for Office 365 AIR pending actions is not documented.
